title: Keep every editor's tag when two save the same product

blocks.text: In the shop's back office, editors tag products by hand while a nightly job adds seasonal tags. Nobody holds a lock while editing: an editor may sit on a product page for minutes. Since the job started running during office hours, editors report tags that "didn't stick": they saved, saw the tag, and an hour later it was gone. Every product row already has a `version` column that nothing uses yet.

items: `addTag(...)`: add one tag and save it, trying at most `ATTEMPTS` times;
`save(...)`: write the new tags, unless someone else saved the product since it was read.

blocks.text: Read products with `load(...)`. The other writers keep the `version` column the way your `save` does. When you're done, no writer's tag is lost, whoever saves first. About fifteen lines in total.
The tests run each editor on its own connection to an in-memory H2 database, and use the `Pause` to let another writer save between an editor's read and its save.

cases.says: tags added one after another all end up on the product, in order
a tag another job saved between the editor's read and save is still there afterwards
two editors running the same code on the same product both keep their tag
an editor whose first two saves lose to other writers saves on the third try, on top of their changes

origin.section: A Version Column Turns a Lost Update into an Update Count of 0

concepts: A version-checked UPDATE returns an update count of 0 when another writer saved first; the caller reads again before retrying, and every writer increments the version.
